items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: we had a boy named Daniel Braseers(?) which later he became one of the greatest jazz trumpets that is known.

ctx.x: 13, 14, 15. I said I'm going to make this band and I was coming into high school too, so I studied the clarinet and the band what it seems those -- this boy's name, Phineas, Phineas was on the trumpet but he just wasn't playing that music and he was my best friend. I got that old cornet that I had and got -- looked at the chart and got down and started playing.

Now, we had -- in this band, we had -- at one point Albert Heights, a violinist, we had a pianist, beautiful pianist, he come from the southwest part of Washington, then we had a full band and by the way, we had a boy named Daniel Braseers(?) which later he became one of the greatest jazz trumpets that is known. They used to call him Georgetown, and he was in the band. So we were rehearsing and across the street, the man had

to eat a bulldog, he was bad, he wanted / everybody up, but when we were rehearsing, the bulldog, he'd walk in and get right under what's this boy's name, Phineas' feet and stay there. He must have loved what Phineas wasn't playing, because Phineas wasn't playing nothing. And Mama had to whisper, "that/ dumb dog," (unintelligible) Mama said, well, you stay there now and don't let nobody else come in. People coming in the windows and everything, so the dog took care of his business and then people baking cakes and…
